6. He's back. Dylan Cardwell finally recovered from his strained calf injury and made his season debut. The second year big man was up to his standard antics, grabbing rebounds and revving up the crowd. The Kings need his energy and his defense around the rim. He played in short bursts.

5. Needed more. Malik Monk had a brilliant game against the Mavs on Monday, but he wasn't able to back it up two days later. Monk shot 5-for-16 from the field, including a 8-for-7 night from behind the arc. He hit some shots late to finish with 13 points and 3 assists.

4. Strong start. De'Andre Hunter has really turned his season around. After a quiet game in Dallas, Hunter went to work against the Lakers, hitting jumpers and drawing fouls. The veteran wing posted another quality performance, finishing with 14 points and 2 rebounds.

3. Showed some fight. Zach LaVine is still fighting the good fight. The Kings desperately need a consistent 20 point per game scorer to pair with Acuff and draw attention, which LaVine has nearly delivered on in almost every game this season. He finished with 21 points and 2 blocks.

2. Double-double. Domantas Sabonis just hasn't been getting enough shots up. It's partially his teammates fault and probably a little on him as well. Against the Lakers, he battled another giant in Walker Kessler and managed to score 16 points to go with 17 rebounds. Not great, but not bad.

1. Learning experience. Darius Acuff Jr. just had a front row seat to an elite performance from an elite, future hall of fame player in Luka Doncic. Acuff didn't back down. He didn't get caught watching and he put his own stamp on the game, posting 22 points to go with 12 assists and 2 steals.
